zones.name: Myeongdong Street
facts: In the 1950s this street was Seoul's Montmartre. War-weary poets and painters packed its tearooms and cheap bars, and people called it the Republic of Myeongdong.
Under Japanese rule this whole district was renamed Meiji-machi. After liberation in 1945 it took back its Korean name — Myeongdong, the bright town.
The grand old theatre on this street opened in 1936 as a cinema called Meiji-za. Today it's the Myeongdong Art Theater, a national stage for Korean drama.

zones.name: Cathedral Hill
facts: Myeongdong Cathedral, finished in 1898, is Korea's first Gothic church — its bricks were fired in twenty different shades by Korean and Chinese craftsmen.
Through the 1970s and 80s this cathedral sheltered Korea's democracy movement. Protesters who reached its steps were, by unspoken rule, left alone inside.
This hill was once Myeongnye-bang, where Korea's first Catholics gathered in secret in the 1780s — decades before any missionary arrived.

zones.name: Namdaemun
facts: Namdaemun Market has traded on this ground since 1414 — six centuries, some ten thousand stalls, and the longest hotteok lines in Seoul.
The market grew up around Sungnyemun, the great south gate built in 1398 — Korea's National Treasure Number One stands just beyond the stalls.
Come before dawn and this market is already roaring — wholesalers here start at 3 a.m., as they have for generations.

zones.name: Hoehyeon
facts: That stone building is Shinsegae's main store. It opened in 1930 as Mitsukoshi Keijō — the very first department store in Korea.
The writer Yi Sang ended his famous 1936 story 'Wings' on that department store's rooftop, with the cry: let us fly, just once more.

zones.name: Euljiro
facts: Euljiro avenue is named after Eulji Mundeok, the general who crushed a million-man invasion in the year 612.
Beneath your feet runs a maze of underground arcades built in the 1960s and 70s — shopping streets that double as civil-defence shelters.
Euljiro's back alleys are Seoul's workshop: tiny shops that can machine, print, or weld almost anything — locals say you could build a tank here.

zones.name: Namsan Foothills
facts: The slope rising ahead is Namsan. For five hundred years, beacon fires on its peak flashed military news across the whole kingdom in a single night.
Namsangol Hanok Village nearby keeps five aristocratic houses and a time capsule buried for Seoul's 600th birthday — sealed until the year 2394.
The cable car up Namsan has been running since 1962 — Korea's very first, and still the sweetest three minutes of skyline in Seoul.

zones.name: Cheonggyecheon
facts: Cheonggyecheon spent forty years buried under a concrete highway. In 2005 Seoul tore the road down and brought the stream back into daylight.
This stream runs eleven kilometres through downtown under twenty-two bridges — at night the banks light up and the whole path becomes an evening promenade.

zones.name: Myeongdong Station
facts: Toegye-ro, the avenue above the station, is named after Yi Hwang — the Joseon scholar whose face is on the thousand-won note in your pocket.
When the Migliore fashion tower opened by Exit 6 in the late 1990s, this corner became the new front door of Myeongdong almost overnight.
